subject: axolotl
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.
reasoning:
I'm planning the chibi axolotl design: a big head, short pale pink body, finned tail, four stubby limbs with digits, and three frilly gill stalks on each side, scaled down to roughly 0.3m long and 0.1m tall.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure — hips as root, a spine chain of two joints leading to the head, a jaw joint, tail chain, legs, and gills — mapping out exact 3D coordinates for each joint and planning how the head sphere and jaw will attach and position relative to the spine.

Still refining joint placement...

I'm shaping the tail fin outline so it flares outward beyond the tube radius at top and bottom, tapering to a point, with a thin 0.004 thickness and rigged to a single bone near the tail's end.

I'm positioning a small dorsal ridge near the top of the body, checking that it sits flush where the body's radius meets the floor, and connecting it smoothly into where the tail fin begins.

Now I'm picking color values, starting with a pink body tone.

Still defining colors...

I'm setting up belly sectors for the sweep geometry, assigning color zones that follow the body and tail chain, then sketching out the front leg bones as short splayed chains going outward and forward from the shoulder joints on each side.

Adding wrist and finger geometry...

I'm setting up a generic leg function with digit direction angles fanning outward-forward for front legs and outward-backward for hind legs, then checking the floor clearance so digit tips don't clip below ground. Next I'll place tiny black bead eyes on the top-sides of the head for a chibi look.

For the eyes, I'm computing the head ellipsoid's surface height at a given x,z offset so the eye sits flush against the curved head, with bigger chibi-style pupils and a small white highlight sphere for shine.

Now I'm figuring out where the jaw seam meets the head surface so I can trace a smile curve along that boundary, computing the z-depth at various x positions to keep the mouth sweep hugging the face.

Working out blush disc placement and sizing on the cheek surface, then computing nostril positions by solving for where they sit on the head's ellipsoid shape, and starting to plan the signature gill stalks along the rear sides of the head.

Building the stalks as bezier curves with a slight upward-lifted control point, then sweeping thin rounded tubes along them in bone color. For the frilly filaments, I'm computing perpendicular directions off each curve's tangent so I can place small spikes alternating on both sides of each stalk.

I want them feathery, tapering shorter toward the tip, colored hot pink, but 324 pieces is way too many parts, so I'm cutting down to around 96 by reducing sample points per stalk.

Computing spike tips by offsetting along the curve's tangent direction, with a forward fan of spikes at the stalk tip. Tilting the gill stalks back and outward from the face, then scattering dark freckle spots on the back and head using small flattened cylinder geometry.

Also planning a belly stripe via sector tagging on the body sweep, and setting up the spine chain's radius profile from hips to head so the neck blends into the head sphere.

Now I'm defining the spine and tail chains with their joint names, confirming the tail has the right number of named joints for its catmull spans, and anchoring both chains to the hips root joint so they share a starting point.

For the limbs, I'm setting up arm and leg chains with shoulder/elbow/wrist naming (and hip/knee/ankle equivalents), assigning parent joints from the spine or hips depending on front/hind, and giving each a sweep profile to create limb thickness.

I'm adding a small flattened sphere for the paw pad at the wrist, lighter-colored spike tips for toes, and glossy black bead eyes with a highlight for the chibi look, plus a pale lower jaw with a tiny tongue sphere tucked inside the mouth.

Now I'm rethinking the head and jaw geometry so the upper skull doesn't overlap the lower jaw region, considering whether to use a hemisphere shape for the head's upper half and let the jaw piece cover the open bottom, while weighing whether an open gap would be visible when the mouth is animated.

Computing eye placement using the surface helper functions, I get the eye sitting around y=0.083 given the x and z offsets, with the sphere radius nudging it slightly outward for a natural look. For the smile, I'm checking where it falls relative to the jaw boundary at y≈0.038-0.04 to make sure it sits correctly on the face surface.

Now I'm plotting the smile curve as a set of points across x from -0.04 to 0.04 with a slight upward curl, then writing a helper function for the gill spikes using bezier curves swept along the stalk with flat and round caps, followed by a loop to place the frills.

For odd k I'll only add one spike along ±Q, keeping it simple. At the tip I want a small tuft of three spikes fanning out from the curve's endpoint, and a tiny sphere nub at the base to suggest a gill stalk. Now I'm moving on to the digits function, then the hand and legs setup with role and angle parameters.

For toe placement, I'm computing each digit's tip position as an offset from the wrist point using angle phi and length 0.024, with the base anchored near the wrist. I'm adjusting the fan angle so front toes point forward-outward and reconsidering whether hind toes should angle backward or also forward-out to match a real axolotl's stance.

Now I'm working out the leg joint coordinates for both hind and front legs, placing the foot, knee, and hip points with appropriate x/y/z offsets so the legs sweep naturally from the body, then setting the tapering radius along the leg segments and toe dimensions. I'm starting to define the dorsal fin extrusion with its outline points and position along the back.

Still writing fin outline...

I'm deciding to simplify the tail fin for now, setting its pinkish fin color and skipping extra details like ridges, spikes, or dark outlines to keep things manageable. Then I'm attaching the spot pattern to the body surface using the sweep result, and confirming the final code just needs the random generator imported from the builder library with no glow effects needed.
